compatibleChanges.rationale: The client admits the diagnostics GET at send time, then receives and writes its body after release. The HTTP request and error framing are unchanged.

Adds the optional developerDir field: a local client's DEVELOPER_DIR, overlaid on the env of commands the daemon spawns for that request. A released daemon ignores the unknown meta key and keeps its own environment, exactly as before; a released client never sends it, so the new daemon inherits its own environment for that request. The remote HTTP surface strips it. Also adds the optional leaseRetainOnClose field, sent only on lease_allocate when the caller opts in: a released daemon ignores the unknown meta key and releases the lease on session close as before, and a released client never sends it. Adds the optional providerCredentialFingerprint field: a digest of the local caller's provider credential variables, which the daemon compares with its own on lease_allocate. A released daemon ignores the unknown meta key and allocates as before; a released client never sends it, so the new daemon skips the comparison. The client sends it only to a local daemon, and the remote HTTP surface strips it. #4511 adds the optional scriptPublicationId string, which a new client sends only on a remote open --save-script to a daemon that reports the script-artifacts capability. Any other request keeps its previous meta.

#2747 adds the 'screen-recording-contact-sheet' literal for the PNG that `record contact-sheet` publishes beside the recording it read. DaemonArtifactType already widens to `(string & {})`, so an artifactType value outside the known set was always valid on the wire; the literal only sharpens the type hint for code that opts into recognizing it. A released peer that does not know it never requests that field in a download and parses the artifact record by its `field`, so it carries the sheet as an unknown artifact instead of failing. #4511 adds the session-script literal the same way. A released client downloads it like any other file artifact named by its field; only a new client, which asked for remote script delivery, gives it a special destination.

#2246 selects a file or directory destination once. Directory downloads stage and safely extract beside the destination, propagate timeout cancellation through both operations, and atomically rename the complete top-level entry; returning that local path is client-only state. The GET /artifacts/:id request and response framing, and every existing file artifact call site's behavior, are unchanged. #4511 passes every download parameter, including the new client-local maxBytes, through to the downloader instead of copying each field. The GET /artifacts/:id request and response framing are unchanged.

Adds the optional providerCredentialFingerprint parameter to agent_device.lease.allocate, forwarded only when the request meta carries one, which the client sets only for a local daemon. A released protocol-2 daemon ignores unknown JSON-RPC parameters, and a request without a fingerprint keeps the previous payload byte-for-byte. The signature also names the client request as DaemonWireRequest and the response as the kernel DaemonResponse instead of the daemon package aliases; only compile-time type names moved. It now composes the envelope through buildDaemonRpcRequest in @agent-device/contracts/lease-scope, which takes the request id from its caller; the client supplies the id it supplied before (the request meta id, else a fresh one), so envelope construction preserves method, params and id. Separately, credential fingerprint lookup now trims the provider name on both client and daemon. A whitespace-spelled provider can therefore add a fingerprint that the released client omitted; this changes fingerprint presence, not the envelope or optional parameter contract.

#2110 read the optional providerApp lease-allocation parameter into the existing flags bag; #2494 reads the full provider-allocation flag set into that same bag through the shared readLeaseAllocateProviderFlags projection, so the reconstructed req.flags handed to prepareSession match what the line transport forwards for free. Released protocol-2 clients omit these and follow the unchanged allocation path; no existing field is required or reinterpreted. The optional retainOnClose boolean parameter is read into meta.leaseRetainOnClose; a released daemon ignores it and keeps releasing on session close. Reads the optional providerCredentialFingerprint lease-allocation parameter into request meta, so a local caller over HTTP gets the same credential check as over the socket. A daemon with an auth hook treats every HTTP caller as remote and strips it, as it does developerDir. Released protocol-2 clients omit it and follow the unchanged allocation path; no existing field is required or reinterpreted. Reads or forwards the optional devicePin allocation parameter. Released clients omit it; older daemons ignore it. Existing fields keep their meanings under ADR 0006. Validates the optional devicePin metadata through the shared parser before dispatch. Existing valid pins and requests that omit a pin keep their request projection. Malformed pin objects now fail clearly with the existing INVALID_ARGS envelope and invalid_device_pin reason instead of a later TypeError. This repairs validation of an unreleased optional field; routes, authentication, framing, and existing fields are unchanged under ADR 0006. #4171 records a request that names no session in daemon-only request state: a missing or blank session, or meta.sessionExplicit false with no named flag. A missing name becomes default, a blank one keeps its literal as released daemons did, and the literal default from a client stays. Lease params gain an optional sessionExplicit, which a released daemon ignores. A released client that names no session on a provider lease through the command method now gets a normal INVALID_ARGS error with reason REMOTE_SESSION_REQUIRED, and no peer misreads a payload.

DaemonError is now declared as an alias of NormalizedError, whose members were already field-for-field identical (code, message, cause, hint, diagnosticId, logPath, logPathUnavailable, diagnosticsRecord, retriable, supportedOn, details). No wire byte changes; only the declaration text moved.

details.dispatched is a new OPTIONAL field inside details, which was already an open record: an older peer ignores the key and every existing field keeps its shape. It carries no | unknown for whether a failed interaction reached the device (the dispatch-disclosure golden table).

#1801 and #1862 client-side only: this reads optional daemon error metadata, most recently the structured `cause`. Parsing of every previously read field is unchanged, so a released daemon's error payload is accepted exactly as before.

Inlined `decodeURIComponent`+catch replaced by the shared `decodeUriSegment` (packages/daemon/src/server/http-request-target.ts), which is listed and byte-identical in behaviour: the same artifact ids decode, and an undecodable id still resolves to the empty id the route rejects.

Implementation-only daemon changes under ADR 0006: #3753 passes the runtime host environment into archiving; #4165 uses a bounded, abortable Node pipeline and validates the declared byte length, with idempotent reader release after completion or failed setup. The handler waits for file readiness before setting headers and starting the pipeline, so open errors use the existing JSON error response. Setup errors clear artifact-only headers first. Successful status codes, headers and artifact bytes retain their existing contracts. Failed or incomplete streaming reads close the HTTP transfer instead of hanging; released clients already treat an interrupted download as failure. Routes, authorization and error JSON shapes are unchanged, so no peer must parse a new payload or send a new field. Implementation-only follow-up to #4165 under ADR 0006: response close cancels artifact preparation and streaming through an internal AbortSignal. Shared builds continue for other downloads. The existing streamed failure helper now owns the same pre-header JSON error and post-header connection destruction. Successful status, headers, bytes, routes and authorization retain their existing contracts; disconnected clients receive no new payload. A response that has finished writing is not cancelled by its normal close event, so successful pipeline completion keeps its existing success semantics. Caller cancellation is normalized to the existing request_canceled error instead of forwarding caller-supplied reasons. Artifact expiry and download deadlines keep their existing reasons. The shared HTTP disconnect helper preserves typed cancellation on aborted requests and unfinished response closes. Directory preparation counts inventory and download callers together, so one disconnected download cannot abort an inventory caller's build; successful response fields and authorization stay unchanged. #4912 reads the existing x-agent-device-lease-id request header. A download of an artifact that a lease produced needs that lease id, else it fails with the existing 401 REST error shape and reason LEASE_OUTPUT_MISMATCH. Released clients since 0.21.28 send the header from the request that produced the artifact. A caller that omits it fails clearly and misreads no payload. Unleased artifacts keep their tenant rule. The size-mismatch failure reads artifact_size_mismatch from its ReasonTable row, preserving the published reason value.

#3753 threads the daemon runtime's host environment into the same archive spawn from the inventory route. The JSON body it writes and the error path are unchanged; no peer-visible field moves. #4912 reads the existing x-agent-device-lease-id request header. An artifact that a lease produced is listed only to a request that sends that lease id; other entries and the JSON body shape are unchanged. A caller that omits the header sees a shorter list and parses it as before.

#1801 and #1862 lift optional metadata onto the normalized error, most recently a redacted structured `cause`. No previously emitted field changes shape or value, and peers that do not know the field ignore it.

#1862 client-side only: this rehydrates the new optional structured `cause` when present. Released daemons that omit it follow the unchanged path, and no request field or existing response field is narrowed.

#2198 slice B teaches the client to read the `upstream` link a proxy's /health already nests. The field is optional and additive: a daemon or proxy that does not send it parses exactly as before, and no request shape changes. readHealthPayload reads the same top-level fields through readHealthLink and additionally the nested `upstream` object when present; a payload without it yields the previous shape.

#2198 checks every link a command RPC crosses for protocol skew. #2650 caps a retry health probe at the request's remaining deadline. Health payload parsing and protocol mismatch refusal are unchanged; released peers still receive the same RPCs. #3178 threads the caller's optional AbortSignal through so a canceled call cuts a probe already in flight instead of waiting it out: the signal is client-local, never serialized, and the GET /health request and payload are unchanged. The mismatch refusal now names both versions and the side to upgrade in its message, with a new hint and a client-local upgradeSide detail; the comparison it makes, the /health request, and the refusal's code and existing detail fields are unchanged, and nothing new is serialized. It now flags the proxy link explicitly, carrying only the proxy's service, rather than inferring it from that name, so a proxy reporting an empty service is still named as a proxy; the comparison and the /health request are unchanged. The new optional callback is local to the client. Daemon and proxy protocol checks and the accepted health response are unchanged.

#2198 context: adds one optional field to the value this DAEMON-INTERNAL gate hands its own route handlers — sessionNamespace, the caller's tenant plus whether the daemon partitioned that caller's session names. Nothing about it is serialized: no request header is read that was not read before, no response field is added, and a refusal keeps the same 401 {ok:false,error,code} REST body sendRestJsonError already sent. What it enables is a refusal DROPPED, never one added — an unattested (client-declared) tenant no longer has the <tenant>: prefix rule applied to it, because scopeRequestSession never applied that prefix to its sessions either. A released peer that now gets 200 where it got 401 is getting the ndjson record it asked for and already parses. The route also passes its ingress signal to the authorizer, so a held auth hook stops at the same deadline or disconnect; the request, response and status framing are unchanged. An auth-hook or tenant-trust refusal answered after the hook now goes through the request owner's commit gate, so a deadline that passed first answers with its own typed expiry; refusal status and body shapes are unchanged.

#2198 context: widens the authorizer callback's result by the same optional sessionNamespace field, so the route can put its tenant question to session-tenant-scope instead of re-deriving the rule locally. The callback is supplied by createDaemonHttpServer inside this process and never crosses the wire; a caller of the route sends and parses exactly the bytes it did before.
The existing locator and NDJSON response keep their shape. Only the server storage lookup and lease authorization change.

#2266 adds the additive harmonyos-instance lease backend literal and #3229 the macos-app literal. Protocol-2 peers ignore a new backend unless it is explicitly requested, and an older daemon refuses macos-app with its existing unsupported-backend error; existing iOS/Android/HarmonyOS values and payloads remain unchanged.

#2266 derives the optional runtime platform from one shared vocabulary, adding harmonyos without changing existing iOS/Android payloads. Older peers can refuse the new value with the existing validation error.
#2266 broadens runtime-hint validation to accept the additive HarmonyOS platform value; existing protocol-2 runtime hints remain valid and unchanged.

#2894 lets an iOS runner start outlive the caller whose deadline gave up on it, so a progress event can arrive after the response ended. The sink now also skips a response whose writable side has ended, next to the destroyed check it already had. No byte written to a live response changes: the envelope framing and payload are untouched, and a released client never sees an event it could not have received before.

#4441 replaces the one 5-minute timer over a whole upload with the preparation aggregate that bounds it, and hands that aggregate's signal to the attempt. The request a peer parses is unchanged: same route, method, the headers buildUploadRequestHeaders produces, the piped payload and the 200/308 handling. A progressing upload may now consume the shared ten-minute aggregate instead of the former five-minute per-attempt ceiling. Connection, header and body-inactivity phase limits stop stalled work sooner; retries and resumes never restart the aggregate. A protocol-2 daemon or proxy parses the same requests, while client-side timeout and retry timing deliberately change. Its only callers run inside uploadArtifact's aggregate, so it no longer opens a second copy of that deadline: it requires the aggregate's signal and drops the timeout message and hint that the outer deadline always preempted. The optional client-local handoff checks ownership when the send starts. Peers receive the same HTTP messages.

#2650 adds an optional daemon instance ID to health metadata or reads it when present, #3047 adds an optional hostArch the same way, and #3229 adds an optional leaseBackends list the same way. Older peers ignore the added fields, and new clients keep probing legacy peers that send neither; existing fields and RPC envelopes are unchanged. #4511 adds an optional capabilities array the same way. Released clients ignore it; a new client treats an absent array as no capability.

#2650 adds an optional instance precondition header. Released peers do not advertise an instance ID, so a new client probes them on every command and never sends the header; older clients omit it and keep their existing RPC behavior.

The health-probe budget includes requester loading and response completion. The caller AbortSignal joins the probe timer only in-process; caller cancellation remains distinct from probe expiry. No signal, timedOut flag, request route, auth header or accepted health payload field changes on the wire, so released daemons and proxies parse and respond as before (ADR 0006). Client-only admission guards the actual health request handoff. The GET path, auth headers, response statuses and health payload accepted from existing peers are unchanged. The client deadline now bounds admission as well as the request. HTTP messages stay the same.

Clients name a held agent-device lease in an optional x-agent-device-lease-id request header on upload, artifact download and request diagnostics HTTP calls, so a gateway can route them. Released daemons ignore unknown request headers and the proxy forwards only its allowlist, so routes, bodies and responses parse as before; with no lease held the request is unchanged (ADR 0006).

The ticket PUT keeps its route, method, headers and body. The optional client-local handoff checks ownership when the send starts. Peers receive the same HTTP messages.

#4441 ends the direct-upload sequence when a transfer phase's own budget expires, instead of re-preflighting for a fresh ticket or falling back, because a second attempt would be permission that budget already refused. Preflight, ticket PUT and finalize requests are unchanged in route, method, headers and body, so a protocol-2 daemon parses everything it parsed before; it just receives no further legs once the caller's aggregate has expired. Its signal is now required, because the preparation aggregate is always the one passed down, and it is read directly; no request changes. The optional client-local handoff checks ownership when the send starts. Peers receive the same HTTP messages.

#4441 drops the hint that named the removed 5-minute timeout, and an expired transfer phase is no longer treated as a transport break, so this route is not re-entered by a fallback after the client's own budget ended the attempt. The POST /upload request itself is unchanged: same method, headers, chunked body and response parsing. A protocol-2 daemon sees the identical request in every case that completes, and no further request in a stalled one. The unreachable timeout message and hint are no longer passed, and the aggregate signal is required. The optional client-local handoff checks ownership when the send starts. Peers receive the same HTTP messages.

The mapper now takes the normalized error (code plus details) instead of the code alone. A gone resource now answers 404 instead of 500: COMMAND_FAILED with details.reason RESOURCE_EXPIRED (an artifact, upload ticket, uploaded artifact or materialized path id the TTL registry no longer holds) maps to 404. The mapper also takes over the DEVICE_IN_USE human_control_active 423 rule, which statusCodeForDaemonError applied only to a failed response a /rpc handler returned. The rule now also reaches the REST routes and thrown /rpc failures, which answered 500: a PUT /admin/leases/<id> refused during a human-control hold, or a non-streamed /rpc call whose handler throws human_control_active, now answers 423. /admin/* is host-only on the loopback port and the proxy never forwards it, and the host already reads 423 for the same refusal on a returned /rpc failure. No released client branches on 404 versus 500 for these routes: downloadRemoteArtifactFromUrl treats any status >= 400 alike, the upload client fails any non-2xx and decides retries from a typed stream detail rather than the status, the /rpc client parses the JSON-RPC error envelope whatever the status and only special-cases 409, and the proxy passes the status through. The error code, message and JSON-RPC error data a peer parses are unchanged, so a protocol 2 peer reports the same failure it did before.

The REST error body gains two optional fields, reason (details.reason when it is a string) and hint, beside the unchanged ok, error and code; full details are never serialized. The declaration's serialized fields, method names and framing are unchanged; only the compile-time type names in its signature moved, so a peer on protocol 2 parses exactly what it did. #4302 (client-side only): the invalid-response error also gains details.reason 'daemon_response_invalid', so the client can disclose whether the request reached the device; it is raised locally from a reply this client could not parse, and no daemon reads it. That same reason string is now read from DAEMON_TRANSPORT_REASONS instead of a literal in this declaration, so the identifier expression in its body moved; the value it publishes is the identical string and no field, method name or frame changes.

#4441 keeps each attempt under its sequential phase watchdog and corrects its transport lifecycle: the connect ceiling now ends at actual socket or TLS-handshake establishment, body progress counts only transport writes, and an early response reads the accepted answer to its end, then destroys and joins the owned file/request pipeline and retires this attempt's phase watchdog before resolving or starting the redirect/resume attempt, so a completed hop's timers never reach the next hop. The outgoing-request phase observation now comes from @agent-device/host-kit/transport's observeClientRequestPhases, which listens to the same socket, TLS-handshake and finish events and is removed when the attempt settles. Bytes on the wire are unchanged: same route, method, headers, body framing, resume-offset handling and redirect limit. Only this client's own sequencing and deadlines moved, so a protocol-2 peer parses exactly what it parsed before. Request-body progress is now each non-empty request write that completes without an error, which Node reports once the bytes reach the local kernel, instead of drain, which fires only after a write returned false. The write wrapper passes every argument and the backpressure result through, so the bytes and framing on the wire do not change. That completed-write observer is host-kit's transport owner, which also stops reporting after the response starts, the signal aborts or the request is destroyed; no request changes. The attempt composes that write owner with the phase observer once per request and disposes both when it settles.  Duplicate success disposal and abort-reason mapping are consolidated without changing precedence. The sole response-path pipeline join remains before outcome or next hop; URL, method, authentication, payloads and framing remain unchanged. Its two refusal errors now read details.reason from UPLOAD_TRANSFER_REASONS instead of literals in this declaration, so only the identifier expressions moved; the values published are the identical strings and nothing a peer sends or parses moves. The optional client-local handoff checks ownership when the send starts. Peers receive the same HTTP messages. The client starts the network watchdog at admission and explicitly hands off streamed headers before releasing it. Request headers, route, body framing and response parsing are unchanged.

#4518 and #4661 change client-side destination selection. Authorized destinations keep precedence. Fallbacks reject NUL names, and ordinary captures reject explicit non-string names and Windows drive-qualified basenames under Windows path rules. Daemons send the same artifact fields with the same framing.

The /rpc body limit is now DAEMON_REQUEST_MAX_BYTES (64 MiB), the one request limit the socket transport, the proxy default, and client writers share, raised from 1 MiB. A larger limit refuses nothing a released client sends; a new client refuses a request over 64 MiB before sending it, and a released daemon still answers anything between 1 MiB and 64 MiB with its own -32700 refusal, as before.

Implementation-only validation repair: a supplied retentionMs is validated before request projection instead of silently dropping fractions or malformed values. Unsupported durations now fail clearly with the existing INVALID_ARGS envelope; released clients can parse that normal command error. No route, authentication, method or wire field changes; no protocol bump under ADR 0006. #4171 records a request that names no session in daemon-only request state: a missing or blank session, or meta.sessionExplicit false with no named flag. A missing name becomes default, a blank one keeps its literal as released daemons did, and the literal default from a client stays. Lease params gain an optional sessionExplicit, which a released daemon ignores. A released client that names no session on a provider lease through the command method now gets a normal INVALID_ARGS error with reason REMOTE_SESSION_REQUIRED, and no peer misreads a payload. The 0.22 lease-id fix reads optional leaseId, tenantId (or tenant), runId, leaseProvider (or provider), leaseBackend (or backend), deviceKey and clientId params, so an install on a leased session sends that session's lease id and its labels are checked. A released daemon ignores the unknown params; a released client never sends them, and on a leased session it gets the normal UNAUTHORIZED LEASE_SESSION_MISMATCH error instead of a misread payload. #4935 compares both aliases of a label with the lease, so a request that sends two aliases with different values gets the same error. No param, route or response field changes.

Rejects internally incompatible selectors in the unreleased optional devicePin field. Valid pins and omitted pins retain their projection; impossible identity/platform combinations now return the existing INVALID_ARGS envelope with invalid_device_pin. This is validation of malformed input, with no protocol bump under ADR 0006.

Tracks the actual metadata declaration instead of its obsolete narrowing waiver. devicePin is an additive optional request field: released clients omit it, older daemons ignore it, and existing metadata fields keep their meanings under ADR 0006.

#4434 moves the actual Node Host/socket base-origin constructor from upload-http into shared ingress validation. It now requires one valid Host authority and derives the scheme from the socket instead of forwarding headers. The adopted publicOrigin migration changes deployment authority configuration, not the upload ticket URL string, authentication headers, body fields, 308 range framing, or finalize format that protocol-2 clients parse. Clients send the returned absolute URL as before. Configured origins are selected separately by the daemon constructor; no existing payload field is removed or reinterpreted.

#4434 accepts optional query components on the existing POST upload, preflight and finalize routes. Existing query-free paths and methods resolve identically; direct-upload IDs still exclude the query. This broadens accepted request targets without removing a route or changing any response framing under ADR 0006.

#4441 adds finite server-side ingress budgets to the existing upload routes: a 600-second aggregate and a 120-second body-inactivity ceiling admitted per request, renewed only after body bytes pass the bounded JSON reader or file writer, and stopped at body completion so post-body work observes just the aggregate, plus explicit daemon listener ceilings: a 30 s header ceiling and a request ceiling derived from the header ceiling, the connections-checking interval, the upload aggregate and a margin. Routes, methods, request fields, response fields, status codes (including the 308 resume framing) and ticket/artifact payloads are unchanged, so a released peer parses and answers exactly as before. The route also passes its ingress signal to the authorizer, so a held auth hook stops at the same deadline or disconnect; the request, response and status framing are unchanged. Expiry is also checked on the monotonic clock before a ticket is created, a chunk offset is committed and an artifact is registered, and an expired exchange ends with the same typed error answer; status codes and body shapes are unchanged. Every answer, ticket publish and registration now commits through the request's single commit gate; a newly created preflight ticket is removed when its answer is refused. Status codes, headers and bodies are unchanged.

#4511 adds the optional scriptPublicationId string and scriptRevision number, which a daemon sets only on a session-script artifact for a remote recording. A released client ignores the unknown fields and downloads the artifact like any other file named by its field; every existing field keeps its meaning.

#4441 adds an optional signal to the auth hook context, aborted when the authorized upload request expires or its client disconnects. The field is server-internal to the hook module the operator loads; no wire request or response field changes, so a released peer parses everything as before.

#4441 adds the upload ingress signal to the internal authorizer callback the upload routes call. It is not a wire field; routes, headers, bodies and status codes are unchanged, so a released peer interoperates as before. An auth-hook or tenant-trust refusal answered after the hook now goes through the request owner's commit gate, so a deadline that passed first answers with its own typed expiry; refusal status and body shapes are unchanged.

#4441 moves the upload routes' existing authorize call into one helper: the same command 'upload', the same per-route positionals and the same token/auth-hook gate, now under the ingress signal. No request, response or status framing changes for a released peer. An auth-hook or tenant-trust refusal answered after the hook now goes through the request owner's commit gate, so a deadline that passed first answers with its own typed expiry; refusal status and body shapes are unchanged.

Adds the optional marker field (pass, fail, warn or skip) to a command progress event, set on a doctor check line. A new daemon sends the line uncolored with its marker, and a new CLI colors the marker after escaping the text. A released CLI ignores the unknown field and prints the message, which is a complete uncolored line. A released daemon never sends the field, and colored its doctor lines itself when its stderr was a TTY or FORCE_COLOR was set: against a new CLI those colored lines now print with their color codes shown escaped (for example \u001b[32m), and uncolored lines print as before. The event type, status and message are unchanged, and no route, status or framing changes.
#4518 client-side only. The optional stagedFile setting affects only local writing. The request, headers, and response framing are unchanged.

Clients name a held agent-device lease in an optional x-agent-device-lease-id request header on upload, artifact download and request diagnostics HTTP calls, so a gateway can route them. Released daemons ignore unknown request headers and the proxy forwards only its allowlist, so routes, bodies and responses parse as before; with no lease held the request is unchanged (ADR 0006). Client-only, implementation-compatible error repair: supported /artifacts downloads still return HTTP 200 with the same bytes, request headers and artifact framing. Redirect/error statuses now fail clearly instead of saving their bodies as artifacts; interrupted error responses settle with the existing COMMAND_FAILED category and numeric statusCode. The bounded body is local diagnostic context, not a new peer payload. Once the diagnostic prefix holds 65,536 characters, the client stops reading the error answer and drops the response; error status and diagnostic contents are unchanged. Released daemons already return 200 for successful artifact downloads, so supported skewed peers parse the same successful framing (ADR 0006). #4744 then catches a failure of the local cleanup that runs after a failed download and reports it as a warning diagnostic, so it can no longer surface as an unhandled rejection; the caller still receives the download's own error. The request, its headers, the response handling and the framing are unchanged. The HTTP request then moves unchanged into requestRemoteArtifact, which this function calls with the same file destination as before; a session script is fetched into memory through that same request.

#4518 client-side only. The optional stagedFile setting selects local staging for a recording download. The request, headers, and response framing are unchanged. An optional client-local callback controls when a file or directory download starts. The GET route, headers and response framing are unchanged.

Passes the in-memory fetchRemoteArtifact to the session-script owner instead of the file download. Which artifacts are requested is unchanged, and the wire fields are unchanged; the client no longer adds a repeat warning to its own output. The GET /artifacts/:id request, its headers and the response framing are unchanged, so a peer on the same protocol sees the same bytes. Materialization forwards the client-local download callback to file downloads and script delivery. It consumes the same artifact and receipt fields.

A script version is fetched into memory, capped at 8 MiB, and committed by the local script publisher under the record lock; a version no newer than the record is answered from the record with no warning. The client reads the same artifact fields (field, artifactType, artifactId, scriptPublicationId, scriptRevision) and requests the same artifact route. The GET /artifacts/:id request, its headers and the response framing are unchanged, so a peer on the same protocol sees the same bytes. Script delivery forwards the optional client-local handoff when fetching a version. It consumes the same artifact fields and preserves version ordering and local publication.

Removes the unanswered open's record through the record owner instead of a direct unlink. The request still carries meta.scriptPublicationId and omits the caller path, and the response is read for the same scriptPublicationId field.
Removes the client-local repeat member and the export; the type never left the client. No request field, response field, route, status or header changes.

#4518 and #4661 change client-side delivery. Record stop keeps its request destination and cwd fallback behavior. The client can skip an unusable destination and append a local reason and warning after parsing the daemon response. The daemon protocol still uses the same request fields, headers, and response framing. The response download loop forwards the optional client-local handoff through its endpoint. It reads the same artifact inventory and preserves local destination behavior.

Removes the github-actions-artifact variant. A new client never sends it. No local daemon ever materialized it: it always failed with UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION. The url and path variants are unchanged.

Adds the session-lease-id capability: the daemon refuses a request on a leased session that does not send that lease's id, with UNAUTHORIZED and reason LEASE_SESSION_MISMATCH (field leaseId). readDaemonCapabilities filters to known values, so a released client ignores the new string. A released client that relied on the daemon filling the lease id from the session gets that normal command error and misreads no payload. The current CLI already sends the saved connection's lease id. No request or response field changes shape.
The server-internal path resolver takes a storage namespace. No HTTP request or response field changes.

Admission controls client-side artifact and diagnostics requests after an error. The remote error projection consumes the same fields and does not require a new field from the peer. Hosted callers can suppress remote diagnostic localization through a client-local option. Accepted response framing and all transmitted RPC fields are unchanged. The client admits the diagnostics GET at send time, then receives and writes its body after release. The HTTP request and error framing are unchanged. Failed batch receipts use the same response fields and artifact IDs. The client admits only the receipt GET handoff and preserves the daemon error envelope.
An optional client-local callback controls when an artifact GET starts. The callback is never serialized.
This client-local type requires the endpoint URL for downloads and carries the optional admission callback. It adds no HTTP fields.
An optional client-local callback controls when an in-memory fetch starts. The GET route, headers and response framing are unchanged.
The file and directory download paths inherit the client-local handoff through their endpoint. Routes, headers and body framing are unchanged.
An optional callback admits the request locally. It is never serialized into the method, URL or headers.
The optional client-local callback admits the GET just before send and releases while the body is read. The method, path, headers, status and body framing are unchanged.
